history.period: 13th century CE (some sources say 13th-14th century; ASI information board)
history.summary: IDENTITY UNVERIFIED — the CSV row 'Shiva Mandir, Bhilai' is generic and dozens of neighborhood Shiva shrines exist in Bhilai; this file documents the best-known referent, the Mahadev Temple at Deobaloda in Bhilai Charoda, described as a historical landmark of Bhilai. It is an ancient east-facing sandstone Shiva temple built by the Kalachuris (ASI information board: 13th-14th century; Wikipedia: 13th century CE), a protected monument under the Archaeological Survey of India. Built in Nagara style, it survives with a garbhagriha housing a ~1.5-ft Shiva linga and a pillared navaranga mandapa; the shikhara is missing. Legend says it was built in six months (hence '6 Maashi' or 'Chhamahi' temple) — one version says the mason fled naked into the temple pond mid-work when his sister arrived, leaving the dome incomplete. A kund in the courtyard is believed by locals to connect via a tunnel to Arang (no archaeological evidence). Mahashivratri draws devotees from nearby villages with a small fair.

town_description: Deobaloda is a village in the Bhilai Charoda municipal area of Durg district, Chhattisgarh, on the Raipur-Durg corridor. It is known principally for its 13th-century Kalachuri-era Mahadev temple, an ASI-protected monument. The surrounding region is semi-urban, between the industrial city of Bhilai and the state capital Raipur.
